title: Adaptive ops sparklets and credentialed ephemeral runners
creator: Leah Mitchell
description: Build a lightweight, policy-gated 'sparklet' runner platform that converts runbook steps into short-lived credentialed tasks. Sparklets are tiny ephemeral agents that execute approved runbook actions inside a constrained environment (IAM-scoped, network-narrowed) and emit structured audit events. Goal: reduce mean time to remediation for common support actions while preserving safety and auditability.
background: Support teams frequently need to perform short, repeatable remediation steps (rotate keys, restart worker pools, invalidate cache). Engineers currently copy/paste runbook commands and rely on manual credential handoffs. Prior efforts (runbook taskification) produced a task model but lacked a secure ephemeral runner and canonical telemetry. This ticket implements the runner piece plus integration with the task catalog and Console traces.
scope: In scope: runner binary, KMS/Vault short-lived credential flow, RBAC gating, runbook-to-sparklet transpiler for simple steps, telemetry hooks into Console, dry-run simulation mode. Out of scope: full UI for step authoring (handled by PM backlog), autoscaling GPU-bound runners, and integration with third-party incident platforms in this sprint.
acceptance_criteria: Sparklet binary can execute a defined subset of runbook actions (restart service, run SQL update in read-only sandbox, clear cache) with ephemeral credentials issued for <= 15 minutes
Every sparklet execution emits a structured audit event (requestor, step-id, git-pr, input hash, exit code) that surfaces in Console activity for >30 days
RBAC policy blocks any non-approved step variants; policy test suite demonstrates enforced deny for at least three forbidden actions
Dry-run mode simulates changes and produces identical telemetry without side effects
End-to-end demo: support engineer triggers a task from chatops -> sparklet runs -> Console shows trace and cost/latency breakdown
implementation_notes: Runner written in Go to keep a single static binary for private deployments; uses POSIX sandbox + seccomp where available
Credential flow: Broker service mints short-lived AWS STS tokens and Vault wrappers for on-prem; runner requests creds over mTLS with client certs issued per-task
Policy gating uses OPA for expression-based allow/deny with rollouts controlled by feature flags
Telemetry uses existing tracer (OpenTelemetry) plus a minimal 'sparklet-audit' JSON envelope to reduce Console parsing work
Trade-offs: starting with a narrow action surface reduces risk; future expansion will require step validators and richer parameter schemas

observability_requirements: Span per sparklet execution with start/end timestamps and host metadata
Audit envelope containing: requester, task_key, step_hash, inputs_sha256, env_version, exit_code
Alert on >3 denied policy hits in 1h for a single user
Sampling: keep 100% audit envelopes for P1 customers for first 30 days
rollback_plan: If production rollout shows unsafe executions, flip feature flag to disable sparklet execution path, revert broker to deny new credential issuance, and surface manual remediation playbooks. Post-mortem within 72h and revert PRs if root cause is code-level.
risks: Misconfigured policy could allow destructive commands if parameter parsing is incomplete
Credential broker compromise would allow elevated access; mitigations include short TTLs and per-task mTLS certs
Console ingestion lag could obscure audit events during incidents
benefits: Faster safe remediation for oncall and support engineers
Standardized audit trail and easier post-incident analysis
Reduced human error from copy/paste and ad-hoc credential sharing
